solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Read aloud savage line 14a

indicators.note: reading something out loud means we hear the sounds of the words rather than their spelling

parts.note: a savage is a beast and a line is a row, so the pair is beast row

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a fierce line from another clue, as if quoting poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 14a is CAFE, so the definition sends you to another clue: the answer is another kind of eatery. BEAST ROW said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clue 14a is a casual eating place, and a small informal restaurant of the French kind is another such place.

clue.text: Critic of broadcaster admitting resistance, a measure of it

indicators.note: letting in, so the broadcaster wraps around the resistance letter

parts.note: the Beeb is a nickname for the BBC
R is the symbol for resistance in physics
the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's critic who shows some restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to resistance, so its unit of measure is the ohm.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Beerbohm was an English essayist and caricaturist who worked as a drama critic.

clue.text: Out to make an impression?

definitions.meaning: workers who are out are on strike, downing tools
something impressive is eye-catching, and coins are made by stamping an impression

explanation.surface: Someone eager to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out on strike and being eye-catching are both described with this one word.

clue.text: Indian bigwig almost arrested

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to run someone in is to arrest them, so ran in

explanation.surface: An important Indian figure nearly taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu queen or a rajah's wife is a person of high rank in India.

clue.text: Bull has arrow's tip removed, next to bow for red giant

parts.note: a bow is an arc, a curved shape

indicators.note: taking something out of the bull's name, so a letter goes missing from it

parts.note: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac

indicators.note: the tip of the word arrow's is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A bull hit by a blunted arrow from a bow, reddening in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red giant' reads like an angry beast, but it is the definition: a type of star.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcturus, in the constellation Bootes, is a bright star of the swollen, cool, reddish type astronomers call a red giant.

clue.text: How long computer takes, especially beginning in frozen state?

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the frost word

parts.note: rime is frost, water in a frozen state
an onset is a beginning

explanation.surface: How long a computer takes, especially when it starts up frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frozen' looks like a computer crash, but it means frost here.
explanation.definitionFit: The delay between an input and the machine reacting is how long a computer takes.

clue.text: After start of trial there's endless time for K

indicators.note: the opening letter of trial
losing its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

explanation.surface: A trial runs on with no end in sight for someone called K.
explanation.definitionFit: K stands for a thousand, and in slang a thou is a thousand pounds.

clue.text: Mean person to be advised that low-quality paper is used for wrapping

indicators.note: the paper wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a rag is a newspaper of poor quality

explanation.surface: A miser told that a cheap newspaper will do for wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasty, unpleasant person is a ratbag in British and Australian slang.

clue.text: Saturated soil study

parts.note: sod is turf, the top layer of soil
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Soaked earth examined closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaked through with water means saturated, as with ground after heavy rain.

clue.text: Ultimately pressed for time in quixotic task

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another, swapping the time letter out

parts.note: like Don Quixote, a knight errant roaming in search of adventure

indicators.note: the final letter of pressed is wanted

explanation.surface: A rushed hero takes on an impractical, idealistic quest.
explanation.walkthrough: ERRANT as in knight errant; its T is swapped for D, the last letter of 'pressed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small job someone is sent out to do is a task, as in running an errand to the shops.

clue.text: Classified advertisement plugged by fancy stores

indicators.note: something plugged has a filling stuffed into it, so the ad is opened up to hold other letters
fancy as a verb hints at reworking the letters of stores into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A classified ad being promoted by smart shops.
explanation.walkthrough: SSORTE, a rearrangement of STORES ('fancy'), fills the middle of A_D.
explanation.definitionFit: Things classified are sorted into categories, as an assorted collection has been grouped by kind.

clue.text: Sentimentality tennis player harbours to embellish 'plucky' reaction when afraid?

parts.note: goo is sentimental gush

indicators.note: harbouring means keeping inside, so the player wraps around the next piece

parts.note: Monica Seles was a top tennis player
to pimp something is to dress it up flashily

explanation.surface: A sentimental tennis star dressing up her nervous reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucky' is a pun: a plucked goose's skin, which ours copies in bumps when we are afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bumps rising on the skin from fear or cold look like the skin of a plucked bird.

clue.text: Salt Lake City, not even parts seen in blackout

indicators.note: the odd parts of blackout are kept, the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A city in Utah seen dimly during a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the Utah city: the salt lake is the Caspian Sea, the world's largest lake, and this capital of Azerbaijan stands on its shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Baku sits on the Caspian, a saltwater lake, so it is literally a city on a salt lake.

clue.text: Morally unacceptable idea one isn't involved in

indicators.note: one is left out of the idea word, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a notion is an idea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shameful concept that one keeps well clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British phrase means something that just is not acceptable, as in 'that sort of behaviour is not on'.

clue.text: Problem of friction sparing hotel restaurant

indicators.note: sparing means leaving out, so the hotel letter is dropped

parts.note: rubbing causes chafing, so to chafe is the trouble friction makes
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Rubbing that troubles a hotel's dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: A small eatery serving drinks and light meals is a kind of simple restaurant.

clue.text: Broth with top third skimmed, vegetarian's base for suitable protein source

indicators.note: the first third, two of the six letters, is taken off the top

parts.note: liquor is the liquid that food is cooked in, a broth

indicators.note: the base of the word, its last letter

explanation.surface: A vegetarian's soup base, skimmed to make a fitting protein source.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing LI, the top third of LIQUOR, leaves QUOR, then add N.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a trade-name mycoprotein food used as a meat substitute, a protein source fit for vegetarians.

clue.text: Is tent forgotten when setting up fanciful small part of atmosphere?

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting up means the letters read bottom to top
left out, so those clue letters are deleted from the fanciful word

parts.note: something fanciful is imaginary, not existing

explanation.surface: A tent left behind while camping in a fantasy world.
explanation.walkthrough: NONEXISTENT less IS TENT leaves NONEX, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble gas present in air in minute traces is a small part of the atmosphere.

clue.text: Remarkable honesty, yours and mine included, marks ____?

definitions.text: Remarkable honesty, yours and mine included, marks ____?

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the shuffled honesty letters
re-marked letters of honesty are put into a new order

parts.note: what belongs to you and me is ours
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A striking display of trust, shared by us all, is what the blank describes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkable' shuffles honesty, and 'included' puts the second piece inside the shuffle. The whole clue fills its own blank: trusted honesty marks such a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement relying on people being truthful without supervision, such as paying into an unattended box, rests on remarkable trust.

clue.text: Impudent tot interrupts a choral session

indicators.note: breaks into, so it goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a sing is a session of choral singing
a tot is a sum, from tot up

explanation.surface: A cheeky child disrupting a choir practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a child; it is a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Presumptuous and arrogant behaviour is cheeky or impudent.

clue.text: Fellow feeling wary, holding bug well up

indicators.note: keeping inside, so the wary word surrounds the rest

parts.note: shy means wary

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tap a phone is to bug it
my and well are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Feeling for someone nervous with a bug welling up.
explanation.definitionFit: Compassion, sharing another's feeling, is the literal meaning of fellow feeling.

clue.text: Support the object with promise to pay underhand as a good sign?

parts.note: a prop is a support
it is the pronoun for an object
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt
underhand and sly both mean sneaky

explanation.surface: Backing something with a secret promise of money, hoping it is lucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Done favourably, in a way that bodes well, as a good omen would.

clue.text: To arrange exhibition on walls needs a bit more than this large shed

indicators.text: needs a bit more than this
indicators.note: the phrase is the answer with one more letter, so a letter is taken off

parts.note: to hang art is to put a show on gallery walls

explanation.surface: Putting on a show needs more room than this big building.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is HANG ART short of T, the 'bit more' that would be needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A large building for housing aircraft is a big shed.

clue.text: Shop to serve as carrier for China?

parts.note: to be something is to serve as it
a tray carries china, crockery

explanation.surface: A shop doubling as a shipping company to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is capitalised to look like the country; it is crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them, so to turn them in.

clue.text: Adult games with kiss as climax

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult
PE, physical education, is school games
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Grown-up play rounded off with a kiss as the high point.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or peak of something is its climax, as at the summit of a career.

clue.text: I'm thinking Nancy's friend is not unsavoury?

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective, the answer is a noun for a taste; the question mark flags the looseness

parts.note: um is the noise someone makes while pausing to think
in Nancy, a French city, a friend is ami

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a friend called Nancy is a decent sort after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a woman's name; it is the French city, so the friend is French.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fifth basic taste, the meaty savoury one of broths and soy sauce, so it is anything but unsavoury.

clue.text: Crack motor-racing team not lapped by European twice

indicators.note: the letters wrapping around the team word are taken off

parts.note: equipe, French for team, is used of motor-racing teams

indicators.note: the European letter is used two times

explanation.surface: A racing team narrowly avoids being overtaken by a European rival twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like an adjective for the team; it is a noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark or jibe, the same as a clever one-liner.

clue.text: Hood caught by hunter at night

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an owl hunts by night

explanation.surface: A hooded criminal caught by someone who hunts by night.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk's hooded garment, or the hood itself, is a cowl.

clue.text: Computer services supporting organisation of global security measure

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: the UN, ... Nations, works for global security
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: IT support for a global security agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard quantity such as a metre is a unit, a measure of amount.

clue.text: Deform egg or lay monstrous one

indicators.note: deforming changes the shape, so the letters of egg or lay are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A hen urged to produce a misshapen egg or just lay a freak.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque carved creature on a church roof is a monstrous figure, often a waterspout.

clue.text: Give nod to Charlie and Jack released from prisons here and in N America

indicators.note: letters let out of the prison words are deleted

parts.words: prisons here and in N America
parts.note: can and joint are both slang for a prison, one here and one in North America
C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet and J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: Two inmates freed from jails on both sides of the Atlantic get the nod.
explanation.walkthrough: C comes out of CAN and J out of JOINT, leaving AN and OINT.
explanation.definitionFit: To anoint someone is to choose them as successor, giving them the nod of approval.

clue.text: Cavalier treatment of soil tray

indicators.note: treatment works the letters of soil tray over into a new order

explanation.surface: A careless way of dealing with a tray of earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' looks like the adjective 'offhand'; here it is a Cavalier, a supporter of King Charles I in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cavaliers backed the crown against Parliament, so each was a supporter of the monarchy.

clue.text: Camp for men only curtailed vision

parts.note: a stag do is for men only

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the eye word is lost

parts.note: the eye gives vision

explanation.surface: A men-only camp with limited views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like a place to stay; it is the adjective meaning theatrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp behaviour is exaggerated and theatrical, the same as being overly dramatic.
